lines.text: Squirrel wants to buy acorns. But acorn prices change every day.
lines.say: Squirrel wants to buy acorns. But acorn prices change every day.

lines.text: Squirrel could wait for the perfect day. Squirrel never knows the perfect day.
lines.say: Squirrel could wait for the perfect day. Squirrel never knows the perfect day.

lines.text: So squirrel buys a little every month, no matter the price. That's dollar-cost averaging.
lines.say: So squirrel buys a little every month, no matter the price. That's dollar-cost averaging.

lines.text: When acorns are cheap, the same money buys more. When they're expensive, it buys fewer.
lines.say: When acorns are cheap, the same money buys more. When they're expensive, it buys fewer.

lines.text: Over those two months, squirrel paid 200 dollars for 15 acorns. About 13.33 each, less than the 15 dollar average price.
lines.say: Over those two months, squirrel paid two hundred dollars for fifteen acorns. About thirteen dollars thirty-three each, less than the fifteen dollar average price.

lines.text: It doesn't promise profits, and prices can fall. But it takes the guessing out.
lines.say: It doesn't promise profits, and prices can fall. But it takes the guessing out.

lines.text: Squirrel explained dollar-cost averaging. Squirrel would like one follow.
lines.say: Squirrel explained dollar-cost averaging. Squirrel would like one follow.
